subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: A customer brings in a locked flagship phone with a physically scratched-off IMEI label and requests a complete software wipe, offering triple your normal fee. According to best workshop management practices, what is the most legally protective course of action?
options: Accept the job immediately to maximize shop profit margins.
Accept the job but only record the customer's first name to maintain anonymity.
Request valid proof of ownership (like a purchase receipt), and decline the repair if they cannot provide it, logging the incident.
Flash the phone using a generic aftermarket firmware to completely bypass IMEI network checks.
questions.explain: Accepting highly suspicious jobs (such as unlocking phones with wiped IMEIs or zero proof of ownership) can implicate the technician in processing stolen property. Refusing the job and logging it legally protects the business from police theft disputes.

questions.q: If an unfamiliar individual hastily enters the workshop requesting an aggressive software pattern-lock bypass and full factory data reset, why must you rigidly demand and record their government ID and proof of purchase first?
options: To secretly acquire their personal data to artificially expand the shop's marketing contact list.
To deliberately slow down shop workflow to justify charging higher hourly reset rates.
To completely ensure the workshop is not legally implicated in aiding the bypass of security on stolen merchandise.
Because standard Android operating systems physically cannot be factory reset without scanning a digitized ID.
questions.explain: Bypassing passwords or screen locks on stolen devices constitutes aiding a criminal act. Stringently verifying formal ID and device ownership severely mitigates legal liability and completely deters thieves from using your shop.
